newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 15.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

New Australian soccer coach Terry Venables conducted his first training session this week as his side prepares for the four-nations tournament, which is designed to let Venables assess Australia's local soccer talent in preparation for the team's upcming World Cup qualifiers. Page 17.

Australian Rugby League chairman Ken Arthurson has expressed concern at the possibility of Channel Nine broadcasting free-to-air Super League games for the upcoming season. Nine's main sporting competitor, Channel Seven, is expected to win the rights for the match of the round on Monday nights. Page 17.

Australian rugby union winger Damian Smith's desire to be re-located to Sydney and play for New South Wales in this year's Super 12 series has led to his former State team, Queensland, seeking legal action. The Queensland Rugby Union says Smith is under contract and will not be released. Page 14.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In-form South Australian batsman Darren Lehmann has been selected to replace the injured Mark Waugh for tomorrow's one day match against Pakistan. The match also sees the return of Paul Reiffel who has been included at the expense of the struggling Tom Moody. Page 50.

It was every boat for itself on Sydney Harbour yesterday, as an 18-foot boat competing in an international tournament was clipped by a Manly ferry, which caused the boat to capsize. The crew escaped serious injury from the incident. Page 49.

A new craze has hit the diving boards around Australia's pools and waterways in recent months - synchronised diving. The new sport, which is raising many eyebrows, has been accepted into next year's world championships, which could lead to its eventual inclusion in the Olympic Games. Page 49.
THE AGE

Australian Open Tournament director Paul McNamee has come out to defend the balls which have been used at this year's championships after two days of controversy. Many of the top players have complained that the balls used are too soft, disadvantaging power hitters, such as Boris Becker and Goran Ivanisevic, who have both made their feelings known. Page C12.

Jennifer Capriati's comeback stumbled yesterday as she was beaten by lowly ranked American Jolene Watanabe. Capriati, who has faced a turbulent last 18 months, broke down and cried during the post-match interview after her shock loss. Page C12.

In line with its recent reduction of teams in the competition, the National Basketball League has opted for a six team finals series this year. The NBL announced that the move is part of its strategy to become a more successful super league. Page 8.
THE HERALD SUN

Following Australia's recent poor form in the one-day series, coach Geoff Marsh has called in "spin doctor" Terry Jenner to help the team's struggling trump card, Shane Warne. The spinner was mauled by West Indian batsman Brian Lara in Australia's loss in Perth on Sunday. Page 78.

Champion pacer Golden Reign has been involved in a freak accident, which will rule it out of several up-coming races. The horse was found in a paddock with wire from an electric fence wrapped around his rear hind leg. Page 71.

Up-and-coming Australian tennis star Lleyton Hewitt made a courageous debut losing to Spain's Sergi Brugurea in the Australian Open yesterday. Hewitt, a 15-year-old from Adelaide, has been labelled a star of Australia's next generation of tennis players. Page 76.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Former socceroo and current Brisbane strikers star Frank Farina is considering taking over the national women's team. The offer, which is a four-year deal, would see Farina build up the team for the 1999 World Cup and 2000 Olympics. Page 62.

Australian basketball star Luc Longley makes his long awaited return to the NBA today after a seven-week lay off after a shoulder injury. The Chicago Bulls centre will play a role in the team's home game against the Washington Bullets. Page 54.

Melbourne Cup winning trainer Bart Cummings has unveiled plans for his star horse Saintly. The horse will trial at Randwick in January, then travel to Melbourne where it will attempt to win its second consecutive Australia Cup at Flemington. Page 55.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
